title: Reverse a List in Groups of k

concept.title: Reverse one group at a time, and stop when fewer than k nodes remain
body: Cut the list into groups of `k` nodes and reverse **each complete group**; a last group with fewer than `k` nodes stays as it is. You already know how to reverse a list segment in place; the difficulty is to do it for many groups and to keep every group connected to the one before it.

Use a dummy node and `prev`, the last node of the part that is already done. In each round: (1) walk `k` steps from `prev` to find the `k`-th node `kth`; if there are fewer than `k` nodes, stop. (2) Remember `group_next = kth.next`, the first node after the group. (3) Reverse the nodes from `prev.next` up to `kth`, making the first node of the reversed part point to `group_next`. (4) Connect `prev` to `kth` (the new first node of the group). (5) Move `prev` to the old first node of the group, which is now its last node.

body.code:
while True:
    kth = prev
    for _ in range(k):
        kth = kth.next
        if kth is None: return dummy.next        # fewer than k nodes left
    group_next = kth.next
    p, cur = group_next, prev.next                # reverse and point the old head at group_next
    while cur is not group_next:
        nxt = cur.next; cur.next = p; p = cur; cur = nxt
    tail = prev.next                               # the old first node, now the last of the group
    prev.next = kth
    prev = tail

body: The trick of starting the reversal with `p = group_next` connects the group to what comes after it without an extra step.

statement: Reverse the nodes of a singly linked list in groups of `k`: the first `k` nodes are reversed, then the next `k` nodes, and so on. If the last group has fewer than `k` nodes, it stays as it is. Change the links, not the values. Print the resulting list.
inputFormat: The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail.
outputFormat: Print the values of the new list on one line.

examples.note: The groups (1 2) and (3 4) are reversed; 5 stays: 2 1 4 3 5.
(1 2 3) becomes 3 2 1; the last two nodes stay: 3 2 1 4 5.

hints: Use a dummy node and a reference `prev` to the node before the current group.
First check that `k` nodes are available; if not, stop.
Reverse the group so that its first node ends up pointing to the node after the group, then reconnect `prev`.

        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)

        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None

            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))


def reverse_k_group(head, k):
    dummy = ListNode(0, head)
    prev = dummy
    while True:
        kth = prev
        for _ in range(k):
            kth = kth.next
            if kth is None:
                return dummy.next
        group_next = kth.next
        p, cur = group_next, prev.next
        while cur is not group_next:
            nxt = cur.next
            cur.next = p
            p = cur
            cur = nxt
        tail = prev.next
        prev.next = kth
        prev = tail

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(reverse_k_group(build_list(a), k))
free_nodes()
